findings.part: measurement / increment I5 (default flip) / revert criteria
findings.claim: The default flip to none is not gated on any measurement, and the revert criteria cannot be evaluated as written. The draft says 'measure first', but I5.depends_on is [I2, I3, I4] only. The Grok planning-only probe it prescribes stops at the first test-spec accept, so it can observe the benefit (minutes) but never the cost (escapes surface at test-red, implement and later).
findings.evidence: [M] Revert criterion (b) needs 'a stage control on the same cell', but owner decision 7 says the E2E harness has no channel to pass --planning-review (test/shiploop_e2e/run.py passes no run option), so no stage control can be run. The only controls are the two 1.21.0 runs, which ran a different engine version without the probe. [M] stage-clock.md says stage times vary about 2x between runs of the same model, and each cell is n=1. 'Escaped defects the baseline review caught' is a counterfactual; both observed expensive revises happened with review on. [M] On the draft's own numbers none lands at 26.8-30.3 min on Grok, and 30.3 (72.7 minus the children clock of 42.4) is over the owner's 30. Criterion (a) says a window over 30 'is not by itself a revert'. So the change can ship, give up all planning review, and still trigger 'rethink planning'.
findings.correction: Make the flip conditional in the plan itself: I5 depends on a recorded Grok medium none probe (run twice, to show variance) and on a to-green run read for first-RED outcome, revise count and minutes. Ship none first as an opt-in value with default stage, as a34a6ee6 shipped backchain none. Restate (b) in observables that exist: revise count and minutes to first green on the same host, and defects found in a post-hoc review of the unreviewed documents. Resolve owner decision 7 (a stage control channel) before I5, not after.

findings.part: modes.once expected_minutes / default recommendation / owner decision 6
findings.claim: 'once cannot meet the 30-minute rule on Grok medium: even a free merged review leaves 39.2 of 72.7' is presented as arithmetic fact. It holds only for the widest window (intake to the first test-spec accept, which includes per-item step-plan and test-spec). Whether that window is the right one is open owner decision 6, and the recommendation for none over once rests on it.
findings.evidence: [M] stage-clock.md, Grok: intake 2.1, discovery 1.8, research 2.1, spec 20.0, test-strategy 19.6, plan 12.2 sum to 57.8 min to the plan accept (58.5 with prepare). [M] run-doc-grok-medium-v1210.json Improve minutes: spec 16.03, test-strategy 14.10, plan 6.03, total 36.16 (children clock 33.5). To the plan accept, none leaves about 21.6-24.3 min (22-25 with prepare), under 30. A free merged once leaves the same, and a merged child costing under about 6-8 min would still fit. [M, Grok pass-1 times from report 3: spec 4.7, test-strategy 2.2, plan 1.4, 8.3 in all, so a merged first pass is plausibly in that range and is unmeasured.] Luna stays far over on either reading (the ledger's intake-to-plan-accept figure is 279.9). [M] The once lower bound also mixes clocks: 39.2 uses the children clock (33.5), while none's range includes the exporter clock. On the exporter clock the once bound is 72.7 minus 36.16 = 36.5.
findings.correction: State the once and none conclusions per window definition, each with its clock, and mark 'once cannot fit on Grok' as holding only for the wide window. Settle decision 6 before recommending none over once. Until then call once 'unmeasured, borderline on the narrow window' rather than excluded, and use one clock consistently (36.5, not 39.2).

findings.claim: The quality-cost statement is one-sided. It omits a measured catch of the same defect class the draft says review misses, and the only controlled catch-rate measurement for the plan-stage review. It treats Sonnet 5.5 as 'reviews changed nothing in hello runs', 'removes a small catch' and 'unmeasured'. The SPEC carve-out Basis and the decision record would carry the same omission.
findings.evidence: [M] Sonnet 5.5 battleship (skill-craft 1.16.0), git -C /Users/dadleet/e2e-runs/20261003/batch-sonnet/battleship/work, commit b1e196d 'Plan: add server entry guard so tests import without listening'. Its body reads 'Review: plan lacked an importable server design; tests needing a port would be flaky. Changes: require.main guard and createServer() export noted in plan.md.' That is the same no-loadable-seam class that cost 165.9 min of redo on Luna xhigh, caught at plan review. The planning commits in that run span about 3.6 min (10:25:54 to 10:29:31), so none saves roughly nothing there and loses this catch. The draft's one-constant default applies to every host. [M] docs/shiploop-composition-state-experiments-2026-09-26.md E6b: the planning review with the platform-claim bullet caught seeded plan-stage platform errors 10/15, against 0/15 without it. Under none the review that carries that bullet does not run. The draft cites this only as '[I, one report]' and omits it from the SPEC Basis.
findings.correction: Add both facts, labelled [M], to quality_risk, the SPEC carve-out Basis, the LEARNINGS entry and design-final.json. Replace 'Whether Sonnet loses anything: unmeasured' with 'one catch measured (b1e196d), time saved about zero'. Weigh a default that is one constant for hosts where planning already takes 3-5 min against what it removes, or state explicitly that the owner accepts that cost. Copy the Sonnet battleship run's evidence into docs/experiments/shiploop-planning-review-20261005/ (journal rule: evidence stays in the repository).

findings.claim: stage is described as 'No behaviour change; the control cell and the revert target', but I2 rewrites the Improve obligations in COMMON, the plan duty, the three step-plan duty variants, the test-spec duty and TEST_FACILITY_HANDOFF for every mode. 'Mandatory actual Improve handoff... remains a draft until that loop completes' becomes 'the Improve child the packet's Improve line names reviews them, when this run has one'. So a stage run no longer reproduces the 1.21.0 baselines' packet text. The only byte-identical test (I1) covers I1 alone.
findings.evidence: [M] shiploop_prompts.prompt(stage, *, delegation, backchain_passes) already takes the Backchain mode and renders the catalog at the default, so the precedent passes the mode into guidance.prompt; the draft's 'no planning_review parameter on guidance.prompt' departs from it. [M] The draft itself says 'stage-mode packets change only by those Improve sentences, deliberately shorter'. The plan duty text at shiploop_prompts.DUTIES['plan'] ('submit this producer result to its mandatory actual Improve handoff. The plan remains a draft until that loop completes') is today's obligation. The weaker wording is an unmeasured prompt change in the mode the owner would revert to, and it confounds any stage-versus-none comparison.
findings.correction: Pass planning_review into guidance.prompt like backchain_passes, with the catalog rendering the default, so stage-mode packets stay byte-identical. Extend the I1 'byte-identical for stage' assertion through I2 and I4, which gives a clean control. If neutral wording is wanted, make it a separate prompt increment with its own evidence and a verbose commit.

findings.claim: I0 is specified as the first commit but states things that open owner decisions still decide. It says the default is none (decision 1), lists once as a value (decision 4), and names the test-author probe as a stand-in check (decision 5, which is also I3 and 'may land in parallel'). It also edits the S-9/S-10 table row to say Improve children are 'read against the run's recorded planning_review', which no increment implements in the E2E harness.
findings.evidence: [M] test/shiploop_e2e/metrics.py only counts directories under improve/ ('improve_children'), run.py has no verdict on them, and the consumer table says the harness needs no change. Only skills/shiploop-e2e-audit/harness/workflow_review.py is changed (I2). The 2026-10-04 precedent (9747d769) came after the owner had decided the option and its default. [M] The parity test splits at the first '**S-10 carve-out' and reads to '**S-11', so it reads both carve-outs. The new text avoids '--backchain-passes X' and 'defaults to X pass', so the regexes stay green, but the first carve-out's pinned wording must be edited carefully (edits a and b).
findings.correction: Do not write I0 until decisions 1, 4 and 5 are answered. Put the probe sentence into I3's own commit as a SPEC edit, or make I0 conditional on decision 5. Make the table-row edit (c) true by implementing the recorded-mode read, or drop it.

findings.part: increments I4 (once) and I5 dependencies / owner decision 4
findings.claim: once (I4, large, about 19 files) is justified as 'the fallback if live none runs show escapes', but the draft's own revert criterion (b) reverts to stage, never to once. I5 lists I4 in depends_on while its own text says 'I4 landed unless the owner drops once'. The mode has no measured purpose under the 30-minute rule on the wide window (at least 36.5 min on Grok, at least 213 on Luna).
findings.evidence: [M] Draft: revert (b) 'revert the default to stage', revert (c) applies only if once is the default; I5 depends_on [I2, I3, I4]. I4 spends 564 B of the 9,216 B contract budget (CONTRACT_BUDGET in shiploop_loop_contract.py), shrinking the host-writable opening for the plan child to about 3.5-3.9 KB, where size refusals have already cost minutes (the 12,448 B contract note). It also needs the I4-only machinery (covered_stages, a script-written scope, a covered-results block). Its minutes are unmeasured.
findings.correction: Per KISS, defer I4 until a none probe shows escapes, or until the owner picks once as the default. Remove I4 from I5's depends_on. If it stays, make the fallback path (b) name once. While once is deferred, I1 should not accept or record a value that behaves as stage (a once or none run recorded in I1 but executed as stage until I2/I4 is a recorded option that lies).

findings.part: increments I3, I4, I5 (commit and journal obligations)
findings.claim: Only I0-I2 name the verbose commit message and journal entry. I3 adds two prompt sentences (test-author and step-plan) and I4 changes PLANNING_REVIEW_FOCUS, the plan prompt and the composed Improve prompts, yet each specifies only a change note.
findings.evidence: [M] The owner's global rule: commits that change prompts get a verbose message with the key learning, the evidence (numbers and the evidence file) and the related commit refs, and the journal is updated in the same commit as the result. The draft's I3, I4 and I5 rows list no LEARNINGS.md edit and no commit-message requirement.
findings.correction: Add 'verbose commit with key learning and refs' and a LEARNINGS.md status line to I3, I4 and I5 (the flip is where the quality-cost evidence belongs).

findings.part: mode none packet text and exit-criterion carrier
findings.claim: The none sentence 'Before you call it done, confirm each Done-when condition against the files you wrote, after your last edit' largely duplicates text already printed in every mode. Under the owner's primary rule the stand-in carrier is therefore unchanged model self-confirmation, not a new check, and the draft should say so rather than list it among what 'stands in' for the loop.
findings.evidence: [M] shiploop_navigator._goal_lines prints for every stage: 'Done when (confirm each before calling done; keep going until all hold):' followed by the stage's done_when. Only 'after your last edit' is new. The prompts-concise-meaningful-change rule says cut ineffective detail and keep obligations.
findings.correction: Trim the none sentence to what is new ('no Improve child follows this result in this run'). State in the carve-out and decision record that the exit criterion is carried only by the producer's own confirmation plus the script gates at complete, and name that this is the unmet half of the owner's 'iterate until a stated check confirms' rule. The draft's SPEC text already says no script-run check covers the semantic criteria, so this is a wording fix.

findings.claim: The ledger's L2 (Improve single pass at the planning stages) is not recorded as a considered alternative, though it is the only lever that keeps part of the review catch. The Change-admission dispositions R1-R15 should say why it is not a mode.
findings.evidence: [M] ledger-account-final.json L2: gross 100.3 min on Luna (about 89.5 net), gives up 2 of 5 warranted fixes (both test-strategy), and is an engine change (required_trivial_reviews=2 in the navigator, the import validator, an S-10 amendment). On Grok medium its pass-1-plus-overhead cost leaves the window well above 30 [I], so it does not meet the owner's rule either. The L1 lever is worded 'replace with script-run checks plus one review after the first RED or at the end', and the draft makes that replacement review optional owner decision 9 (not in this change).
findings.correction: Record L2 and the L1 replacement review as considered, with the reason each is out of scope (neither reaches 30 min; L2 is a larger engine and SPEC change). Promote owner decision 9 from optional to an explicit accept or reject, because it is the only compensating review the ledger's own L1 specifies.
